lesson: In merge_records, identify duplicate contacts by matching the lowercased email and the calendar day of the updated timestamp, rather than requiring an exact timestamp match.
why: Exact timestamp matching was causing the CRM contact list to retain duplicates of the same person across sync runs.
quote: The key is right - same email ignoring case, same day, that's one contact.

lesson: When duplicate contacts clash in merge_records, keep the record with the highest count of non-empty fields, rejecting the keep-latest approach.
why: Sync jobs strip fields, making newer records emptier and causing phone numbers and company data to be lost when latest wins.
quote: Count the non-empty fields and keep whichever record has more - most-filled wins, no matter which side it came from or which is newer.

lesson: In merge_records, resolve tied field counts by keeping the primary CRM record, and maintain a stable output order of primary records first followed by new incoming records.
why: The existing CRM record is the source of truth when completeness is equal, and contact list ordering needs to remain stable.
quote: Then keep the one from primary - the CRM is the source of truth. And keep the order stable
